title: Build a Prompt Learning Loop - SallyAnn DeLucia & Fuad Ali, Arize
talk_summary: Arize's RISE team presents 'prompt learning': an optimization loop that feeds LLM-judge and human feedback (labels plus free-text explanations of *why* something failed) into a meta-prompt that rewrites the system prompt, iterating against a train/test split. They show a coding-agent case study where adding a rules section to the system prompt improved a benchmark by ~15% and let a cheaper model approach a stronger one's performance.

takeaways.technique: Rules section in system prompts, learned from failures
takeaways.what_they_do: They took a bare coding-agent system prompt with no rules and added explicit engineering rules (error handling, tests accompany changes, align with system design), then measured on a coding benchmark.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we were able to improve by 15% just through the addition of rules
takeaways.numbers: ~15% improvement on a coding benchmark (s-bench light); 4.1 near 4.5 performance at two-thirds the cost

takeaways.technique: Feedback with explanations, not just labels
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of optimizing against a scalar score, they collect correctness labels plus free-text explanations (from human annotators or an LLM judge) pinpointing which instruction failed, and feed that text into the prompt rewriter.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of just the label, it provides the reasoning behind the label

takeaways.what_they_do: They run a second loop on the judge itself: collect cases where the judge is low-confidence (logprobs, jury-of-judges), have humans annotate those, and optimize the eval prompt the same way as the agent prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the left loop only works as well as your eval

takeaways.technique: Train/test split to avoid overfitting prompt rewrites
takeaways.what_they_do: They split failure examples 80/20, optimize the prompt on train, and gate acceptance on test-set accuracy, stopping when a target threshold or max loops is hit.
takeaways.numbers: 80/20 split; 5 optimization loops default, threshold-based early stop

takeaways.technique: Cheap-model substitution validated by prompt optimization
takeaways.what_they_do: They show a cheaper model (4.1) reaching near-state-of-the-art (4.5) coding performance after prompt optimization, at two-thirds the cost, with no fine-tuning or architecture change.

takeaways.technique: Optimize each agent's prompt in isolation
takeaways.what_they_do: For multi-agent systems they optimize each specialized agent's prompt independently rather than simulating the whole pipeline, arguing each agent has its own prompt to learn from.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each of those agents may be specialized. They may have their own prompts that they need to learn from
